turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Right, I'll grab your blood pressure before Dr. Brennan calls you. Arm out straight for me.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh god, it'll be sky high. I was white knuckling the whole way in, the M50 was desperate.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Sure we'll see in a second. My sister is the same in waiting rooms, she gets palpitations and has to step outside, but that's her own worry, not yours.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry. I just, umm, I keep thinking it's something bad.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): One twenty eight over seventy eight, pulse seventy six. That's grand. He'll be in now.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Seventy six, is that too fast? Should I be worried about the heart as well?
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): Not from that number, no. I'll leave ye to it.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello there. I'm Dr. Brennan. What's been going on?

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): It's the tummy. I've these cramps, and my bowels are all over the shop. Sorry, I'm going too fast. It's been a year now, and I googled bowel cancer at two in the morning like an eejit.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll slow it down. Tell me about the cramps themselves.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Low down, kind of gripey. And err, once I pass a stool they ease off. Nearly every time.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Is the tummy bloating up as well, between the pains?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh yeah. Especially after lunch. I look about six months gone by the evening, it's mortifying at the desk.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the stools. Are they hard, loose, or swinging between the two?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Swinging. Constipated for a few days, then it goes loose, like porridge, three or four times in a morning, then back the other way. That's been the whole year.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the stool, or black stool?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No blood. I actually looked, because I was scared. Nothing.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Have you lost weight, without trying?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No. If anything the jeans are tighter with the bloating. I haven't lost weight.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does the pain or the loose stool wake you up at night?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. I wake for the alarm anyway, so I can't really say.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Is night time the dangerous one? That's what the forum said. Am I not explaining it right?
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): What you said isn't a clear yes or no, so I won't treat it as a night symptom. Tell me only what you're sure of. Any vomiting?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No vomiting. I feel a bit sick with the cramps sometimes, but I don't actually get sick.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the waterworks. Any burning, or going more often?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No, that's all grand. No bother there.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Could it be coeliac though? A girl at work was told she had it and she was bloated. Or an ulcer? Or, uh, cancer, honestly?
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Those are fair questions. Bowel cancer is unlikely with no bleeding and no weight loss, but I'm not brushing you off.

[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): What this sounds like is irritable bowel. The muscle in the bowel goes into spasm, particularly when you're under stress, and that spasm is the cramp. When you pass a stool the pressure drops and the pain eases. That's my working impression, not a final stamp.

[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): So the stress is actually doing that to the gut? Work is brutal. I'm a payroll clerk in a hotel and since January I'm there till seven most nights, lying awake thinking about the wages.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): It can wind a sensitive gut up, yes. Stress isn't eating a hole in you. Let me check what you've already tried.

[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): The GP gave me mebeverin, one hundred and thirty five milligrams, three times a day. I took it about a month and I'm after stopping it in March, because I wasn't sure it did anything.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): The chemist put a box of Buscopan in my hand as well, but I never took a single one. Still sitting in the press.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): So the mebeverin is stopped since March, and the Buscopan was never started. Anything else you are actually taking?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Peppermint oil capsules, when I remember. Umm I think they're about two hundred milligrams, maybe twice a day, but I forget half the time. The bottle's at home.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ok. I'll have a feel of your tummy, if you're alright with that.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. It's a bit sore on the left today. Will it hurt? I tense up, I can't help it.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Soft abdomen. Mild tenderness low on the left. No guarding. I can't feel any mass. Bowel sounds are there.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): No mass. So not a tumour you can feel? You're sure?

[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nothing on examination suggests a mass. I still want bloods, because this has gone on a full year. I'll check for anaemia, inflammation, and coeliac disease before I settle on the irritable bowel.

[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): So, saying it back. A year of low cramps that ease after a stool, bloating after lunch, stools swinging from constipation to loose, no blood, no weight loss, heavy stress in the payroll job, mebeverin stopped in March. Does that match?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. That's it. Sorry, I keep leaping ahead with the questions.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Will the needle be awful? How long do bloods take? And if it is coeliac do I have to give up my mam's brown bread forever?

[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Quick scratch, results are usually a few days. We only talk about dropping gluten if the coeliac test is positive, not before. For now, regular meals, ease off the fizzy drinks and the big lactose loads, smaller portions, and a simple food diary for two weeks. That often settles the bloating.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): I do drink a good bit of sparkling water and the odd Coke, yeah. Is the peppermint oil safe to keep on with?

[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Peppermint oil is grand to continue if it suits you, take it with food. I'm not adding a new tablet today. Come back and see me in three weeks and we'll go through the bloods and the diary. Reception will book it on the way out.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Three weeks. Ok. If I see blood, or the weight starts dropping, I shouldn't wait though, should I?

[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): You shouldn't. Blood, weight loss, or pain that turns constant and severe, you ring us or the out of hours the same day. Otherwise I'll see you in three weeks. The nurse will do those bloods now.

spec.situation: Person with cramps relieved by passing stool, bloating, alternating constipation and loose stools for a year; stress at work; denies blood and weight loss after prompting; bloods planned, diet advice.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: No statement of difficulty falling asleep by the patient.
bad.text: Difficulty falling asleep (category=neurological, status=present, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Negative finding asked and answered: no dysuria and no increased urinary frequency ('Any burning, or going more often?' / 'No, that's all grand. No bother there.').
Buscopan was recorded incompletely: patient had a box from the chemist but never took a single one; it was never started.
Peppermint oil current use detail missing: patient takes it only when remembered/forgets about half the time, and doctor advised to take it with food.
The patient reported left-sided abdominal soreness today before examination ('It's a bit sore on the left today').
Night symptoms were specifically queried and remained indeterminate rather than present or absent: patient gave an unclear answer, and doctor stated he would not treat it as a night symptom.
Doctor explicitly said he was not adding a new tablet today.
Safety-net advice was more specific: same-day contact should be with the practice or out-of-hours service if blood appears, weight starts dropping, or pain becomes constant and severe.
Plan detail missing: blood tests were to be done immediately after the visit ('The nurse will do those bloods now').
